questions.question: What did PCA show about the sources and magnitude of variation in the FTIR datasets?

options.A: PC1 explained 83% and PC2 11% of variability, with major loading variation in the 1750–850 cm⁻¹ region
options.B: PC1 explained 11% and PC2 83%, with variation concentrated at 4000–3000 cm⁻¹
options.C: PC1 and PC2 each explained about 50%, with no treatment clustering
options.D: PC1 explained 83%, but loadings showed variation only in the lipid region above 2800 cm⁻¹

questions.rationale: The first component dominated the variance; loadings highlighted a nucleic-acid/protein-rich spectral region for follow-up peak analysis.
questions.evidence_quote: Principal Component (PC)-1 gave a variability of 83% and provided information for the vast source of variation (Figure 1 .A) when compared to PC-2, which had a variability of 11%.

questions.question: Which spectral feature did the authors use to infer early RNA synthesis, and how long did its increase persist after CpG stimulation?

options.A: The RNA-specific ribose peak at 915 cm⁻¹ increased from the first minutes and remained elevated until 2 h
options.B: The DNA phosphate peak at 1238 cm⁻¹ rose only after 6 h and remained elevated for 24 h
options.C: The amide I band at 1639 cm⁻¹ increased at 10 min and persisted through 6 h
options.D: The ester C=O band at 1741 cm⁻¹ increased only after 2 h

questions.rationale: The 915 cm⁻¹ ribose vibration is RNA-specific; its early increase precedes the later DNA synthesis contribution.
questions.evidence_quote: stimulation with CpG DNA has significantly increased this peak value from the first minutes (p < 0.001***). This increase is maintained until 2 h after stimulation

questions.question: What temporal order of nucleic-acid synthesis did the authors infer after CpG DNA activation?

options.A: RNA synthesis predominated through about 2 h, with DNA synthesis beginning from 6 h
options.B: DNA synthesis predominated through 2 h, with RNA synthesis beginning from 6 h
options.C: RNA and DNA synthesis rose simultaneously only at 6 h
options.D: DNA synthesis was absent at all measured times, while RNA increased only at 6 h

questions.rationale: The authors attribute early nucleic-acid changes to RNA and interpret later changes from 6 h as DNA synthesis.
questions.evidence_quote: The time until 2 h after stimulation seems to be the period of extensive RNA synthesis, and as this ceases, DNA synthesis starts from 6 h after stimulation with CpG DNA.

questions.question: How did the total protein signal respond to CpG DNA and LPS, according to the study's summary?

options.A: Both treatments caused an initial rapid increase that leveled off around 2 h post-activation
options.B: CpG caused a steady decline, while LPS caused a delayed rise after 6 h
options.C: Only LPS increased protein, and the signal peaked at 10 min before disappearing
options.D: Neither treatment altered total protein; only RNA and DNA changed

questions.rationale: The abstract and detailed protein analysis report an early rise in both activated groups, with the increase reduced from the 2 h time point.
questions.evidence_quote: CpG DNA and LPS result in an initial rapid increase in the total protein concentration, leveling off two hours post-activation.

questions.question: Which FTIR bands were used to track triglyceride/cholesterol ester content and fatty-acid side chains, respectively?

options.A: The ~1741 cm⁻¹ ester C=O peak and the ~1400 cm⁻¹ COO⁻ symmetric-stretching peak
options.B: The 915 cm⁻¹ ribose peak and the 1238 cm⁻¹ phosphate peak
options.C: The 1639 cm⁻¹ amide I and 1540 cm⁻¹ amide II bands
options.D: The 3000–2800 cm⁻¹ lipid region and 1085 cm⁻¹ symmetric phosphate stretch

questions.rationale: The study integrates the ester carbonyl signal for triglycerides/cholesterol and the COO− symmetric stretch for fatty-acid chains.
questions.evidence_quote: we focused on the ester C=O stretching vibrations represented in the IR spectrum at the peak near 1741 cm -1

questions.question: What treatment doses and post-treatment time points were used to compare macrophage activation by CpG DNA and LPS?

options.A: 1 µM K3 ODN or 0.5 µg/ml LPS, measured at 10 min, 30 min, 2 h, and 6 h
options.B: 0.5 µM K3 ODN or 1 µg/ml LPS, measured at 15 min, 1 h, 4 h, and 12 h
options.C: 1 µM LPS or 0.5 µg/ml K3 ODN, measured at 10 min, 30 min, 2 h, and 6 h
options.D: 1 µM K3 ODN or 0.5 µg/ml LPS, measured only at 2 h and 24 h

questions.rationale: RAW 264.7 cells received 1 µM endotoxin-free K3 ODN or 0.5 µg/ml LPS, and spectra were acquired at four specified time points.
questions.evidence_quote: CpG DNA stimulated group was treated with 1 µM K3 ODN (Endotoxin-free; Integrated DNA Technologies, Belgium), and LPS stimulated group was treated with 0.5 µg/ml LPS

questions.question: What was the study's replicate structure for FTIR analysis?

options.A: Each group was measured in three independent scans per replicate, with five replicates used in analysis
options.B: Five scans per replicate were collected from three independent biological replicates
options.C: One scan per sample was collected across 128 biological replicates
options.D: Three technical scans were pooled into one replicate, with only two replicates analyzed

questions.rationale: The methods distinguish three independent scans whose average constituted a replicate from the n=5 replicates used for analysis.
questions.evidence_quote: Each group was scanned under the same conditions in three independent scans (the average constitutes a replicate n). Replicates (n=5) were used in data analysis.

questions.question: Why did the authors wash and centrifuge cells before collecting ATR-FTIR spectra?

options.A: To remove medium-derived organic compounds and biological fluids that could mask cellular IR features
options.B: To remove intracellular RNA so only DNA-specific signals remained
options.C: To induce cell-cycle arrest and synchronize nucleic-acid synthesis
options.D: To increase the water absorbance that improves the FTIR baseline

questions.rationale: The samples were washed after removing media to avoid external components confounding the bulk-cell infrared spectrum.
questions.evidence_quote: These steps were carried out to remove organic compounds, growth medium, or biological fluids, which can mask the IR spectrum features

questions.question: What shared metabolic interpretation did the authors draw from increased fatty acids, triglycerides, and cholesterol in both activated groups?

options.A: The coordinated increases point to a shared synthesis pathway and de novo lipogenesis
options.B: The increases demonstrate selective lipid degradation and fatty-acid oxidation
options.C: The changes indicate that CpG and LPS block cholesterol synthesis but increase RNA production
options.D: The profile shows uptake of extracellular lipids rather than any biosynthesis

questions.rationale: The authors interpret increases across fatty acids and neutral lipid products as evidence of activation-associated de novo lipogenesis and shared pathway regulation.
questions.evidence_quote: Both activated groups increase the concentration of fatty acids, triglycerides, and cholesterol, pointing out to a shared synthesis pathway and de novo lipogenesis.

questions.question: Which methodological limitation motivated the authors to present FTIR as a complementary rather than molecule-specific assay?

options.A: FTIR provides bulk relative macromolecular information, whereas omics quantifies specific molecules but needs complex preparation that can alter chemical ratios and modifications
options.B: FTIR requires complex sample preparation and measures only DNA, whereas omics directly measures all metabolites
options.C: FTIR cannot detect proteins or lipids, while omics cannot quantify RNA
options.D: FTIR requires living cells on the ATR crystal and is unsuitable for time-course measurements

questions.rationale: The authors frame bulk FTIR as simple and rapid but less molecule-specific than omics; omics preparation may perturb the chemical composition it seeks to quantify.
questions.evidence_quote: Even though the trending "omics" techniques yield precise quantitative data on specific molecules rather than the bulk analysis done by FTIR spectroscopy, they require complex sample preparation steps that can result in alterations of chemical ratios
